prompt: What is a seam, in this lesson?

choices.text: A comment marking code that has no tests yet
choices.why: A seam is in the code's shape, not in a comment.

choices.text: A place where a collaborator is handed in
choices.why: Right. An argument such as carrier or opener, where a test can pass a double.

choices.text: The line where a unit test ends and an integration test starts
choices.why: That is a boundary between layers, a different idea.

choices.text: The join between two commits that a merge produces
choices.why: Nothing to do with version control here.

prompt: price builds its own CarrierClient inside the function body. What can a test no longer do?

choices.text: Call price at all
choices.why: It can call it; every call just reaches the network.

choices.text: Decide what the carrier answers
choices.why: Right. With the client created inside, there is no place to hand in a stub.

choices.text: Measure how long price takes
choices.why: Timing is still possible, and slower.

choices.text: Check the free-shipping rule on the subtotal
choices.why: That check happens before the carrier is asked, so a test reaches it either way.

prompt: Passing a collaborator in as a parameter instead of creating it inside has a grand name: dependency ___ .
In the refusal test, why is the mailer None?

choices.text: The order is stopped before that argument is ever used
choices.why: Right. None is a dummy: required by the signature, and it would blow up if used.

choices.text: Because SmtpMailer cannot be imported in tests
choices.why: It can; step 6 imports it to build an autospec mock.

choices.text: To make the test send real e-mail through the default server
choices.why: None has no send method; nothing is sent.

choices.text: Because place ignores its mailer argument
choices.why: place does use it, after the refusal check.

prompt: A test of the refusal builds SmtpMailer("smtp.example", 25) instead of passing None. What risk does that add?

choices.text: None, the two are equivalent
choices.why: They are equivalent only while the refusal stays above the e-mail line.

choices.text: The test fails to import pytest
choices.why: Building an object has nothing to do with imports.

choices.text: If the check moves below the e-mail, the test reaches a real server
choices.why: Right. It then sends mail or hangs on a timeout, where None would have failed loudly.

choices.text: The refusal is no longer raised
choices.why: The refusal does not depend on which mailer is passed.

prompt: What does StubCarrier do when it was built with an error?

choices.text: It records the error in a list for the test to read
choices.why: That would be a spy; the stub keeps nothing.

choices.text: Raises it when rate is called
choices.why: Right. It raises the error it was given, which puts price into its fallback branch.

choices.text: It calls the real carrier and passes on the error it gets
choices.why: A stub has no network and no logic.

choices.text: It retries twice and then returns the table price
choices.why: Retries are not in the stub, and the table is price's fallback.

prompt: With the carrier stand-in three seconds late and the client's timeout at 2 s, how many seconds of real time did the session take, as printed by time?
Why is the stub's timeout test in the fast layer while the session against the slow stand-in is not?

choices.text: The stub raises the error at once; the real timeout waits two seconds
choices.why: Right. Same branch of price, reached without waiting.

choices.text: Because the stub test checks a different branch of price
choices.why: Both reach the fallback branch.

choices.text: Because pytest skips tests that sleep
choices.why: pytest skips nothing for sleeping.

choices.text: Because the stand-in is written in another language
choices.why: It is Python too; the cost is the wait.

prompt: The spy test compares lines == [the expected line]. What does that catch that "timed out" in lines[0] would not?

choices.text: A fallback that returns the wrong price
choices.why: The spy test does not look at the price.

choices.text: A carrier that answers too slowly for the timeout
choices.why: The stub fails at once; speed is not in this test.

choices.text: A second, unexpected line
choices.why: Right. Comparing the whole list fails on any extra or missing line.

choices.text: An empty log, when price logs nothing
choices.why: lines[0] on an empty list raises IndexError, so that is caught either way.

prompt: Somebody deletes the log(...) call in price. Which of the four tests in test_carrier.py goes red?

choices.text: The carrier's price wins when it answers
choices.why: The carrier answered, so nothing is logged anyway.

choices.text: The table is used when the carrier is down
choices.why: It passes a log that discards lines and checks the price only.

choices.text: The fallback is logged with the reason
choices.why: Right. It is the one test that reads what was logged.

choices.text: A free order never asks the carrier
choices.why: No fallback happens on a free order.

prompt: A spy records calls; with a spy, the ___ reads the record and asserts on it.
Why does test_a_free_order_never_asks_the_carrier need a double that records calls?

choices.text: Because the carrier is too slow to call in a test
choices.why: Speed is not the reason; the point is a call that must not happen.

choices.text: The return value is 0 either way
choices.why: Right. Only the record of calls shows that the paid API was not asked.

choices.text: Because pytest requires a mock when a function returns zero
choices.why: pytest requires nothing of the kind.

choices.text: To check that the CEP was normalised
choices.why: The test asserts no call at all, so no CEP is checked.

prompt: SmtpMailer.send became deliver. With a plain mock.Mock(), the order test passed. Why?

choices.text: A plain Mock accepts any method name
choices.why: Right. It answered send as happily as it would have answered sned.

choices.text: Because pytest caches the old SmtpMailer between runs
choices.why: The test never touched SmtpMailer at all.

choices.text: Because orders.place was renamed too
choices.why: place still called send; that is the bug.

choices.text: Because the rename did not reach the file on disk
choices.why: git diff --stat showed the change.

prompt: With create_autospec(SmtpMailer, instance=True), what error did the order test raise after the rename?

choices.text: TypeError: missing argument body
choices.why: The arguments were never reached; the attribute was missing.

choices.text: AttributeError: Mock object has no attribute 'send'
choices.why: Right. The same error production would raise, found in the fast layer.

choices.text: AssertionError: expected send to be called once
choices.why: The test stopped before the assertion, at the call itself.

choices.text: ConnectionRefusedError from smtplib
choices.why: An autospec mock opens no connection.

prompt: Which of these are true of a plain unittest.mock.Mock()? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: It records every call made to it
choices.why: Right. call_args and call_count read that record.

choices.text: It answers a method name it has never seen
choices.why: Right. mailer.sned(...) succeeded in the capture.

choices.text: It refuses calls that the real class does not have
choices.why: That is create_autospec, not a plain Mock.

choices.text: It sends the call on to the real object afterwards
choices.why: A Mock replaces the object; nothing is passed on.

prompt: What makes FakeOrders a fake rather than a stub?

choices.text: It is in a file called fakes.py
choices.why: The file name is a convention; the behaviour decides.

choices.text: It raises errors on demand
choices.why: Raising on demand is what the stub does.

choices.text: It keeps what it was given and hands out ids
choices.why: Right. It has real behaviour, through a shortcut: a list instead of a table.

choices.text: It checks the calls made to it with assertion methods
choices.why: That is a mock.

prompt: FakeOrders.add starts ids at 0 while the real table starts at 1. Tests using the fake pass. What keeps fake and real in agreement?

choices.text: Code review, since both files are short
choices.why: Memory is the thing that failed; the lesson asks for something else.

choices.text: A mock of the fake
choices.why: A double of a double checks nothing about the real table.

choices.text: Coverage of fakes.py at 100%
choices.why: Coverage says the lines ran, not that they agree with the table.

choices.text: One set of tests run against both
choices.why: Right. Parametrised over the fake and the real implementation, the first-id test fails for the fake.

prompt: Match each real collaborator with a well-known fake.
Match each double to its example in shipquote.
A test is about the price returned for a CEP, and the carrier is in the way. Which double fits?

choices.text: A mock asserting rate was called with the CEP
choices.why: That checks a call, and this test is about a result.

choices.text: A stub
choices.why: Right. It sets what the carrier says; the assertion is on the price.

choices.text: A dummy carrier set to None
choices.why: price calls rate on it, so None would fail.

choices.text: The real carrier, through the lab's stand-in on every run
choices.why: Slow, and a contract test's job, not this one's.

prompt: The names dummy, stub, spy, mock and fake come from Gerard Meszaros's book xUnit Test ___ .
mock.patch("urllib.request.urlopen") did not reach CarrierClient. Why?

choices.text: Because patch only works inside pytest fixtures
choices.why: patch works as a context manager anywhere.

choices.text: Port 9 is reserved and the operating system blocked the patch
choices.why: The port only explains the refusal; the patch failed earlier.

choices.text: The default argument took the real urlopen at import time
choices.why: Right. Defaults are evaluated once, when the function is defined.

choices.text: Because urllib cannot be patched in Python 3.13
choices.why: It can; this is about when the name was looked up.

prompt: A module does from urllib.request import urlopen and calls urlopen(...). The module is shipquote/fetch.py. Which target does the patch need?

choices.text: "urllib.request.urlopen"
choices.why: The module holds its own copy of the reference.

choices.text: "shipquote.fetch.urlopen"
choices.why: Right. Patch the name where it is looked up.

choices.text: "urllib.urlopen"
choices.why: That name does not exist in Python 3.

choices.text: "shipquote.urllib.request.urlopen"
choices.why: shipquote has no urllib attribute.

prompt: How did the missed patch show itself in the run?

choices.text: As a warning that the patch target was not used
choices.why: No such warning exists; that is the danger.

choices.text: As a connection error, three exceptions deep
choices.why: Right. A missed patch fails as something else, or passes against a real service.

choices.text: As a skipped test
choices.why: It ran and failed.

choices.text: As a pass, since the server on port 9 answered
choices.why: Nothing listens on port 9; it was refused.

prompt: The carrier now answers price_cents. What did the four stub tests do?

choices.text: Passed
choices.why: Right. They never talk to the carrier, so its change cannot reach them.

choices.text: Failed with KeyError: 'cents'
choices.why: That was the contract test.

choices.text: Were skipped because CARRIER_URL was set
choices.why: Only contract tests skip, and only when it is not set.

choices.text: Timed out after two seconds each
choices.why: Stubs answer at once.

prompt: Why is a pipeline that never sets CARRIER_URL a problem, if every run is green?

choices.text: Because the stubs then call the real carrier instead
choices.why: Stubs never call anything.

choices.text: Because pytest fails a run that has skipped tests
choices.why: A skip does not fail the run; that is the point.

choices.text: The contract tests are skipped every time, so the contract is never checked
choices.why: Right. A skipped test is not a passing test.

choices.text: Because the token is printed in the log
choices.why: Nothing is printed when nothing runs.

prompt: pytest prints the reasons for skipped tests when given the option -r___ .
A provider's sandbox costs money per call and is down twice a week. Where do the contract tests run?

choices.text: On every push, so drift is caught at once
choices.why: That pays per push and goes red whenever the sandbox is down.

choices.text: Nowhere; the stubs are enough
choices.why: Then nothing ever notices the stubs going stale.

choices.text: On a schedule, with a failure read as stale stubs
choices.why: Right. Nightly against the test environment, as section 10 suggests.

choices.text: Against production, with a real customer's CEP
choices.why: Production is not a test environment.

prompt: A test of place asserts every call in order and breaks when place is refactored with the same result. What is the symptom called in the lesson?

choices.text: The test mirrors the implementation
choices.why: Right. It restates the code, so it fails on changes that kept the behaviour.

choices.text: The double drifted from the real thing
choices.why: Drift is a double going stale; here the code changed shape.

choices.text: The test is flaky
choices.why: It fails every time, for the same reason.

choices.text: The suite is shaped like an ice-cream cone
choices.why: That is about layers, not mocks.

prompt: Put the checklist's questions in the lesson's order.
items: Is the real thing slow, costly or unavailable?
trap: Whether a double is needed at all comes first; how to keep it honest comes last.

prompt: Why are brl and freight never mocked in shipquote's tests?

choices.text: Because they are private functions
choices.why: They are public; that is not the reason.

choices.text: Because unittest.mock cannot replace module functions
choices.why: It can; it is a choice not to.

choices.text: They are fast and deterministic, so the real ones cost nothing
choices.why: Right. A double is for what is slow, costly or unpredictable.

choices.text: Because they have no tests of their own
choices.why: Both have unit tests.

prompt: A new collaborator returns exchange rates from a central bank API that updates hourly. A test of a price in euros must be deterministic. Which double, and what keeps it honest?

choices.text: A plain Mock, kept honest by assert_called_once_with
choices.why: A call assertion checks the call, not the shape of the real answer.

choices.text: A stub with a fixed rate, plus a scheduled contract test
choices.why: Right. The stub fixes the rate; the contract test checks the real API still answers in that shape.

choices.text: The real API, kept honest by retrying when the rate moves
choices.why: Retrying does not make a moving rate fixed.

choices.text: A dummy, since the rate does not matter
choices.why: The price depends on the rate, so it matters.

prompt: Match each failure to the habit that catches it.

pairs.left: A renamed method still called by a plain Mock
A changed answer from the carrier
A patch that misses its target

prompt: Which of these situations are good reasons to use a double? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: The collaborator charges per call
choices.why: Right. Cost per call is one of the checklist's reasons.

choices.text: The collaborator's answer changes with the time of day
choices.why: Right. Non-determinism makes a test pass or fail by the clock.

choices.text: The collaborator is a pure function that returns in microseconds
choices.why: Then the real one is cheaper than a double.

choices.text: You need the collaborator to fail on demand
choices.why: Right. A stub raising an error reaches a branch the real thing rarely takes.

prompt: In the contract-drift capture, what would production have done with every quote?

choices.text: Answered 500 to every customer
choices.why: price catches CarrierError and falls back.

choices.text: Answered with price_cents in the body
choices.why: The client never reads price_cents.

choices.text: Quoted from the table, writing one log line each time
choices.why: Right. The fallback hides the break from customers; the log line is the only trace.

choices.text: Retried the carrier until it answered cents
choices.why: There is no retry in price.
